q1.text: If you had to introduce yourself in one line —
options: Slow to warm up; crowds drain me
I like a crowd, and I'm good at livening one up
I don't say much, but I'm wild around close friends
It depends entirely on who I'm with

q2.text: When the decision doesn't matter much, you —
options: Look at the facts first, feelings second
Go with your gut, fix it later if it's wrong
Ask the people around you what they think
Put it off until it becomes clear on its own
Time alone, reading or watching something
Out with friends, the livelier the better
Tidying the room and putting everything back in place
Wandering somewhere you've never been

q4.text: People most often praise you for being —
options: Gentle and easy to be around
Fun, quick-minded
Dependable — things are safe in your hands
Full of ideas that aren't quite like everyone else's
Show on your face; anyone can tell
Stay inside; you don't let much show
Steady, seldom a big swing either way
Big swings, but they come and go fast

q6.text: In anything you do, you care more about —
options: Whether it actually gets done
Whether you enjoyed the process
Whether it has your own style to it
How other people will see it

q7.text: The first impression you want this name to give —
options: Gentle, clean
Capable, crisp
A little mysterious, keeps some distance
Interesting, memorable

q8.text: Which kind of name do you prefer —
options: Obvious at a glance, generous and common
With a touch of the old, as if from a poem
Cool and rare, unlikely to be shared
Two simple characters, easy to write and say

Bob Marley.bio: A key figure in the global spread of reggae, whose songs often speak of peace and unity.

Lady Gaga.bio: Known for songwriting, stage art and film performance.

Ed Sheeran.bio: Known for folk-pop songwriting, guitar playing and live performance.

Ralph Fiennes.bio: Active on stage and screen, at home in historical figures and complex dramatic roles.

Kate Winslet.bio: Won the Academy Award for Best Actress for delicate performances across many kinds of film.

Christian Bale.bio: Known for rigorous preparation for roles and a shifting screen image.

Matt Damon.bio: Active in commercial and dramatic film, and involved in writing and producing.

Julia Roberts.bio: Long active in Hollywood, known for comedy and drama roles.

Viola Davis.bio: Has won several major honors for powerful work on stage, television and film.

Miles Davis.bio: A jazz trumpeter and composer who repeatedly shifted the style of the music.

Wes Anderson.bio: Built a distinctive film style from symmetrical framing, storybook color and peculiar humor.

Guillermo del Toro.bio: Known for fantastic creatures, fable-like narrative and delicate visual design.

Jean-Luc Godard.bio: A key French New Wave director who renewed film language with jump cuts and self-reflexive narrative.

Ingmar Bergman.bio: Known for films exploring faith, death and intimacy.

Marion Cotillard.bio: Active in French and international film, with many complex roles.

Monica Bellucci.bio: Noticed for performances and screen presence in Italian and international film.

Penélope Cruz.bio: Active in Spanish-language film and Hollywood, and a winner of the Academy Award for Best Supporting Actress.

Celia Cruz.bio: A legend of Latin music through salsa and her signature stage performances.

Javier Bardem.bio: Known for film roles of strong personal presence and an international career.

Björk.bio: Known for experimental music, visual art and distinctive performance formats.

Jungkook.bio: Internationally known through group and solo music and stage performance.

Lisa.bio: Draws global attention for group and solo music, dance and fashion work.

Son Ye-jin.bio: Long active in Korean film and television, with many kinds of roles.

Youn Yuh-jung.bio: Long active in Korean film and television, and won the Academy Award for Best Supporting Actress for an international film.

Kenshi Yonezu.bio: Widely known for pop songwriting, production and anime theme songs.

Hikaru Utada.bio: Broadly influential in Asia through pop songwriting in Japanese and English.

Amitabh Bachchan.bio: One of the most representative actors in Indian film history, with a career spanning decades.

Deepika Padukone.bio: Long active in Indian film and involved in public advocacy for mental health.

Alia Bhatt.bio: Noticed for varied roles in Indian film and for production work.

Rajinikanth.bio: One of the most influential stars in South Indian cinema, known for a distinctive screen style.

Madhuri Dixit.bio: Known for film performance, dance and lasting pop-culture influence.

Shakira.bio: Globally known for Latin pop, dance and cross-language songwriting.

Bad Bunny.bio: Drove the global spread of Spanish-language pop through Latin trap and reggaeton.

Wizkid.bio: A leading figure in Afrobeats who helped take it international.

Burna Boy.bio: Noticed for music blending African rhythms with global pop elements.

Youssou N'Dour.bio: Known for mbalax music and international cultural exchange.

Trevor Noah.bio: Known for stand-up, comedy performance and commentary on international public affairs.

Hou Hsiao-hsien.bio: A key director of the Taiwan New Cinema, known for restrained long takes and writing historical memory.

Tang Taizong.bio: Li Shimin, who created the Zhenguan era and valued taking counsel.

Miriam Yeung.bio: Long active in Chinese-language culture through Cantonese pop and film performance.

Nicholas Tse.bio: Spans music, film, television and the restaurant business.

Mozi.bio: Founder of the Mohist school, who urged universal love and attended to logic and technique.

Qu Yuan.bio: A poet of Chu in the Warring States period and author of the Li Sao; the Dragon Boat festival is linked to him.

Yuan Longping.bio: A pioneer of hybrid rice research, with major contributions to grain yields and agricultural science.

Sima Qian.bio: Author of the Records of the Grand Historian, which set the model of the biographical general history.

Qian Xuesen.bio: A founder of China's space program, involved in building missile and aerospace technology.

Bai Juyi.bio: A Tang poet whose plain language attends to the life of the people and social reality.

Du Fu.bio: A high Tang poet known for attending to social reality and for a deep, grave style.

Zhu Xi.bio: The great synthesizer of Song Neo-Confucianism, long influential on East Asian education and thought.

Nurhaci.bio: United the Jurchen tribes and founded the Later Jin, laying the base for the Qing dynasty.

Kang Youwei.bio: A late Qing reform thinker who advanced debate on reform and modern political change.

Cai Yuanpei.bio: An educator and president of Peking University who urged inclusiveness and academic freedom.

Tu Youyou.bio: Won the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for research on artemisinin.

Hammurabi.bio: Known for the Code of Hammurabi, a key example of ancient written law.

Pericles.bio: A key leader of Athenian democracy who advanced classical Athenian culture.

Ashoka.bio: A major Mauryan ruler who in later life promoted Buddhism and non-violent governance.

Murasaki Shikibu.bio: Author of The Tale of Genji, regarded as an important early novelist of the world.

Ibn Sina.bio: A scholar of the medieval Islamic world whose Canon of Medicine long shaped medical education.

Ibn Khaldun.bio: Deeply influenced the social sciences with his theory of social history and the Muqaddimah.

Saladin.bio: A major medieval ruler known for uniting Egypt and Syria and for diplomatic skill.

Mansa Musa.bio: A ruler of Mali known for wealth, his pilgrimage and trans-Saharan exchange.

Johannes Gutenberg.bio: Improved movable-type printing and advanced the spread of knowledge in Europe.

Simón Bolívar.bio: A key leader of Latin American independence, called the Liberator.

Abigail Adams.bio: An important public figure of the founding era, known for her letters and political views.

Franklin D. Roosevelt.bio: An American president who carried out the New Deal and led the country in the Second World War.

Rosalind Franklin.bio: Provided key evidence for understanding DNA structure through X-ray crystallography.

Aretha Franklin.bio: A leading soul singer known for a powerful voice and musical influence.

Eleanor Roosevelt.role: American public figure and human rights advocate
Eleanor Roosevelt.bio: Took part in United Nations human rights work and helped shape the Universal Declaration of Human Rights.

Golda Meir.bio: The fourth prime minister of Israel and an important early woman leader there.

Desmond Tutu.role: South African bishop and human rights advocate
Desmond Tutu.bio: An important voice against apartheid who advocated truth and reconciliation.

Aung San Suu Kyi.bio: A key figure in the Burmese democracy movement and a Nobel Peace Prize laureate.

Nikola Tesla.bio: Made major contributions to alternating current, electric motors and wireless technology.

Thomas Edison.bio: Involved in the commercialization of the electric light, sound recording and power systems.

Grace Hopper.bio: A compiler pioneer who advanced modern programming languages and software engineering.

Vint Cerf.bio: A key participant in designing internet protocols, called one of the fathers of the internet.

Carl Sagan.bio: Known for planetary science research and for writing about the cosmos for the public.

Kip Thorne.bio: Researches gravitational waves and relativity, and took part in gravitational-wave detection.

Jocelyn Bell Burnell.bio: Discovered pulsars and has long advanced science education and women in science.

Mae Jemison.bio: The first African-American woman in space, with a background in both medicine and engineering.

Demis Hassabis.bio: An AI researcher and technology founder involved in advancing protein structure prediction.

Katalin Karikó.bio: An mRNA researcher who won the Nobel Prize for related medical contributions.

Homer.bio: The Iliad and the Odyssey are traditionally attributed to him.

Dante Alighieri.bio: Author of the Divine Comedy, with deep influence on European literature and the Italian language.

Geoffrey Chaucer.bio: Author of the Canterbury Tales, regarded as a key founder of English literature.

Miguel de Cervantes.bio: Author of Don Quixote, with far-reaching influence on the development of the modern novel.

Fyodor Dostoevsky.bio: Known for psychological depth and ethical thought, above all in Crime and Punishment.

Franz Kafka.bio: A modernist whose work often depicts alienation, institutions and existential impasse.

Chinua Achebe.bio: An important writer of African English literature, writing of colonial experience and cultural change.

Nawal El Saadawi.bio: Used literature and social writing to address women's rights and social structure.

Isabel Allende.bio: Known for novels of family narrative, historical memory and a woman's perspective.

Rabindranath Tagore.bio: A Nobel laureate whose work spans poetry, fiction, music and education.

Khalil Gibran.bio: His poetic prose and philosophical works circulated widely around the world.

Banksy.bio: Known for socially critical street art and anonymous practice.

Georgia O'Keeffe.bio: A modernist known for paintings of flowers, bones and the New Mexico landscape.

Claude Monet.bio: A leading impressionist who valued light and momentary visual sensation.

Salvador Dalí.bio: A leading surrealist known for dreamlike images and meticulous technique.

Auguste Rodin.bio: An important forerunner of modern sculpture, author of The Thinker among others.

Le Corbusier.bio: An important theorist and practitioner of modernist architecture and urban planning.

Zaha Hadid.bio: Known for flowing curves and avant-garde design, and a Pritzker laureate.

Antoni Gaudí.bio: Known for natural forms, colorful ornament and his buildings in Barcelona.

Igor Stravinsky.bio: A major twentieth-century composer who kept exploring ballet, classical and modern musical language.

Sam Walton.bio: Founder of Walmart, who advanced the large retail chain model.

Madam C. J. Walker.bio: An early well-known American businesswoman and philanthropist.

Indra Nooyi.bio: A former head of PepsiCo, long involved in corporate strategy and public affairs.

Susan Wojcicki.bio: A former chief executive of YouTube, long involved in internet products and technology management.

Satya Nadella.bio: Chief executive of Microsoft, who advanced cloud computing and AI.

Ren Zhengfei.bio: Founder of Huawei, long engaged in communications technology and enterprise management.

N. R. Narayana Murthy.bio: Co-founder of Infosys, who advanced India's software services industry.

Carlos Slim.bio: Long invested in telecom, retail and finance.

Sundar Pichai.bio: Chief executive of Google and Alphabet, long involved in internet product management.

Sergey Brin.bio: Co-founder of Google, involved in search and internet technology.

Larry Page.bio: Co-founder of Google, involved in search engines and internet product innovation.

Neymar.bio: Known for dribbling, creativity and a long international career.

Kylian Mbappé.bio: Noticed for speed, scoring and performances in international competition.

Marta Vieira da Silva.bio: One of the most representative players in the history of women's football.

Megan Rapinoe.bio: A World Cup winner who has long advocated gender equality and social justice.

Manny Pacquiao.bio: A world champion across multiple weight classes who later entered Philippine public life.

Tiger Woods.bio: One of the most influential players in modern golf, with many major titles.

Lewis Hamilton.bio: A Formula One world champion active on diversity and environmental issues.

Max Verstappen.bio: A Formula One world champion known for speed and an attacking driving style.

Rafael Nadal.bio: A Grand Slam champion known for his clay-court record and tenacious play.

Novak Djokovic.bio: A Grand Slam champion known for complete technique and a long competitive record.

Mikaela Shiffrin.bio: A world champion and Olympic medalist in alpine skiing.

Hidilyn Diaz.bio: Winner of the Philippines' first Olympic gold medal.

Wangari Maathai.bio: Founder of the Green Belt Movement, who won the Nobel Peace Prize for environmental and peace work.

Anthony Fauci.bio: An infectious disease expert long involved in American public health policy and public communication.

José Andrés.bio: Provides humanitarian aid in disaster zones through projects such as World Central Kitchen.

Leymah Gbowee.bio: Organized a women's peace movement and won the Nobel Peace Prize for helping end the Liberian civil war.
